blocks.content: The Finance Commission acts as the balancing wheel of fiscal federalism in India.

rows: Union Ministries / NITI Aayog (formerly Planning Commission)
Charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India
Allocated out of Central budget allocations
To assist specific states in need of revenue deficit support
To execute plan schemes and national development priorities

items: Article 280 empowers the President of India to constitute the Finance Commission every fifth year or earlier.
The 15th Finance Commission reduced the states' share in the central divisible pool from 42% to 41% to adjust for the newly created Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
Distinction between Article 275 (statutory grants on FC recommendation) and Article 282 (discretionary grants) is frequently tested in UPSC and State PCS exams.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fiscal federalism governs the financial relationship and division of tax powers between the Union and the States in India.
The Finance Commission, constituted under Article 280, acts as the primary constitutional body regulating vertical and horizontal tax devolution.
Vertical fiscal imbalance is mitigated by transferring a designated share of the net proceeds of divisible central taxes to the states.
Horizontal fiscal imbalance is addressed through criteria-based allocations like income distance, demographic performance, area, and forest cover.
Statutory grants under Article 275 are provided to states in need of financial assistance based on Finance Commission recommendations.
